title: This is the app I wanted!!!
review: If you are a plant parent and need something to keep you organized, this is your app. I originally bought a subscription to another plant app starting with a P which I now regret…because its answer for every plant problem is water and light and soil without being specific. This one is VERY specific and is really good about identifying the correct plant If you don’t know what you are working with. But the thing I really enjoy about it is the schedules…it tailors your watering schedule to your plant and takes into account the size, light, soil, type of pot and reminds you to fertilize and mist and snip flowers…just everything. I bought a subscription pretty immediately because I wanted access to all the features, so I don’t remember what comes free and what doesn’t but what is also cool is the progress updates. You can keep records of the soil recipe you used, compare pictures to see how it’s doing, and it has a snooze and skip feature in the event that you check your soil and it’s not ready for watering yet. I strongly recommend this app for anyone who wants to be more organized and diligent with a watering schedule…my only recommendation for an additional feature would be to have something to track when you spray it with bug spray. Great, great app…I look forward to using it for a long time to come!!!

title: Very helpful app but some suggestions…
review:
🪴🪴🪴🪴Edit: I noticed that you added the slow release fertilizer sticks as an option but you cannot change this for an existing plant. 😔 I have 120+ plants and would prefer to use those types of fertilizers but don’t want to have to delete all my plants and add them back and lose all my progress. Can you please push another update that allows you to modify your current fertilizer preferences? ⭐️ 🌟⭐️🌟⭐️🌟

I have been using Planta for several months now and use it daily. I am a premium subscriber and while I do love the app I have some suggestions: it doesn’t seem to update watering schedule based on the amount of times you snooze the action. I live in rural VA and in the spring my houseplants don’t seem to need to be watered as often as the app suggests based on pot type and location. I would have thought the app would develop an algorithm over time but it doesn’t seem it has. Another helpful thing would be for you to be able to take a picture of a plant problem and submit it for review. I have had some issues with my plants that I am not positive are the issues outlined in Dr. Planta so I am not confident I am always treating the condition effectively. I wish that feature was more robust. I would also like to have the option to add light sources that are grow lights as I grow a lot of mine under lights. Overall, I love the app and will likely subscribe for another yearly subscription next year too. 🙂

title: Very helpful, makes me feel confident to buy more plants
review:
I had a few houseplants for awhile but could never remember to water them, and so I didn’t feel like a very good plant mom. I decided to try an app, and I’m happy I chose this one, and I’m happy to pay for the premium version. I find it super helpful with the daily reminders, and the ability to identify plants through the app. 
There are somethings I wish I could do through the app — I wish when you add a plant it would prompt you with questions about the current condition the plant is in, is the soil still moist when you bought it, are there new leaves that haven’t opened yet? Things like that that could help you notice the progress your new plant makes since bringing it home. 
I appreciate the Dr Planta feature but I wish they gave you the option of writing in what the issue is, instead of just giving you a couple of options to choose from. 
Also, I wish you could update a plant’s type after you have entered it as part of your inventory. I think I chose the wrong color variant on one of my plants, and I think I just have to delete it and enter it as the other one? Please tell me if there is a way to change this without deleting it and losing all of the data I had saved for it. 
Overall I’m very happy with this app, and I think the premium features are worth it for a newbie like me. I have learned a lot already and I’ve only had the app for a month. Thanks Planta!

title: Best app out of all the other
review: I was struggling to find an app I kept deleting some because they never notify in time, they never recognized my plant, or their plant spectrum was not broad enough. I really like this app it gives you information about your plant that I never knew. I hesitated on getting the subscription but I’m glad I made the decision on buying it. The plant doctor is so helpful it tells what I’m doing wrong when I didn’t realize that I was doing harm to the plants. I love the schedule misting option cause most of my plants need that and I forget to do that when I live in a dry area. The only reason why I didn’t give it all 5 stars because it has some flaws I hope they can fix. For example live in Los Angeles and the app says the weather here is 70 degrees which in reality it’s either 80 or 90 😣 so I don’t know if that will affect my plants watering at night since it tells me to water them longer than I usually do. Talking about the  watering schedule I wish it has a schedule of setting a LOUD alarm at a specific time because I am a college student the only time I can care for my plant is between 10-11 o’clock am and I know I can’t water them later because of my assignments; another thing is when I water them at night, I learned the hard way, my plants are more prone to pests and bacteria. If anyone is reading this help to get the developers attention to fix this app I really like it.

title: Not worth the subscription
review: It’s ok. But not yet worth the money for the premium subscription. I’m an advanced plant keeper, and my main reason for buying it was to track my plant care so I don’t have to do it manually in my own database, which does save a lot of time. Plus, I like the ability to search plants quickly for different qualities. So I’m enjoying it for some of those things. However, it’s not really there yet. Good things: 1) Fairly nice plant search and plant ID; 2) Nice task tracking features 3) Nice notifications 4) Tasks can be grouped by site, task, or plant, which is nice. 5) Ability to customize plant care for advanced users - nice. Frustrating things: 1) some of the info is just plain wrong. They do allow users to send corrections, but that requires their users to do their research for them — kind of lame. 2) So far, zero support. I’ve contacted them twice but no response. 3) I can’t use it with both my iPhone and iPad because the password/sign in isn’t working to cloud-share info. 4) Plant search is really nice to suggest plants by site conditions, but doesn’t allow multiple filters (such as, only pull up plants that aren’t toxic to pets/kids, etc.) 5) The info is very, very simplified — which is good in some ways, but not in others. A room may have several different lighting zones in it, but Planta just simplifies these into a “room,” and then tells you what would work in there or not. Advanced users would know they need to customize that a lot more, but beginners might not realize that their site still doesn’t get enough light even though Planta says it does. Etc.

title: Needs some work
review: I am a premium subscriber, but I probably will not renew. I have over 100 houseplants. I wish the app would automatically adjust itself if you’re having to water more often. Two of my plants have died from lack of water because Planta is soooo generous with the amount of time between watering. My humidity must be a lot lower or something but if I am actually going around feeling my soil, things are much drier than they should be. I let Planta guide me for a few months and my plants started dying and now I don’t trust the app. I wish it let you also track a little better with health issues and be more specific about what’s going on. Also an option for baby plants/propogation plants that are in water. You don’t have the option of logging a plant unless it is in dirt. Also everything is the exact same soil and fertilizer needs.  and they don’t give a lot of information about your plants. I have to rely on other apps that are free to give me better detailed information. Oh, and the progress thing is REALLY annoying because of the gigantic delay from when you take a picture in the app to when it saves it, it’s ridiculous. I just ignore my progress updates because it takes about an hour to do 20 plants because of the lag. A lot of people ask me for what app I use and I find myself recommending this less and less. If Planta makes some updates to their algorithm, I’ll renew. But the features available and lack of learning from the app, make it not worth the premium price.

title: Great, But could be better
review:
I love this app! I like the easy access to clicking my watering cycle. I like that I can categorize my plants into different rooms they are in. Things to make this app even more worth $35: -I’d like to have the ability to edit the watering cycle to a more specific date. You can only mark today, yesterday, about a week ago, about 2 weeks ago, or not sure/never watered. These are so vague when you add a plant. -if you accidentally mark that you have watered a plant that hasn’t been watered, you can’t edit the watering cycle. I end up having to put a reminder on my calendar. -Maybe adding a calendar to the app would make it easier for us to know which plant needs watering. -when my plant is sick and overwatered, the app still gives me a reminder to water the plant even if it diagnosed it as overwatered. It would be helpful to not have it in the “water” reminders if it is identified as overwatered. Looking forward to more improvements for this app!

UPDATE:
Omg! You actually read my feedback :D this makes me happy and feel heard! Also, thank you for showing me that I can edit the watering cycle and change the date! Looking forward to the grow light options and to the many more additions to this app <3

title: Great app - needs more details
review:
So I’ve been using the free version of this app for a few months and I wanted to try out the premium version so I know when to fertilize and all. I’m glad it tells you when to fertilize, but every plant says “all purpose fertilizer” which honestly if you use that on all of your plants you will burn some roots and kill them. Some house plants need a specific fertilizer. And it’d be cool if there were some natural alternatives in there as well, like banana peel water. Also, add what kind of soil you should use! There should totally be a big soil section, but not one that just says “all purpose potting soil” like, definitely have someone who knows what they’re doing tell you what different mediums to mix for this certain plant. (Coco coir, peat moss, perlite etc.) If you added these small details I’m sure you’d have much more business. The right soil and fertilizer is so important for growth. One more thing, do some quick research on each of your plants to make sure Planta is giving you the right info. I’ve been barely watering my rubber trees and letting them dry out because that’s what planta said, but I just did some research and saw that they need to stay moist during the summer 🤦🏻‍♀️ sooooo, that’s why two of my rubber trees are drooping and dropping leaves. 
Overall, I’m super grateful for this app because I could never keep up with my 47 plants without it, but definitely could use some more details!

title: Great app, still needs improvements
review: I got this app a little over a year ago when my friend bought me my first plant. Since then I’ve collected over 100 plants, worked at several plant stores, and have decided to go to college for horticulture. I do feel like none of this would’ve happened without this app, it gave me a starting point. It made a really complex hobby understandable and easy to follow. I love this app and I recommend it to every single single person that tells me they want plants but don’t think they could keep them alive. However, like the title says, it could use some improvements. First of all, when doing progress updates the app will glitch by popping up your keyboard before getting to the text box. When you scroll down to type too quickly, the keyboard will disappear after you press a letter. Second of all, in the new community section (which I absolutely love) whenever someone likes/replies your comment and the app notifies you, when you click the notification it takes you to the post and doesn’t display the like/comment. And finally a few suggestions that I think would be a good addition: when creating a new site for plants, I’d like to be able to make subcategories for the sites. For example I have plants in multiple houses, so I have 2 different kitchen and living room sites. It’d be nice to be able to categorize the rooms by houses for people like me. Lastly, I would love to be able to create a custom task and set it at an interval. For example, check for pests, remind me every month. Or rotate plant, remind me every two weeks. Thank you for hopefully reading this, and I hope you can make a great app even better.

title: Game changer but needs some improvements
review:
Edit: I know this app is primarily for indoor use - but can y’all add an option for outdoor space like a balcony? During the summer months I love all of my succulents to my balcony but as it’s a lot hotter outside and in the sun versus inside in direct sun I figure my plant friends have slightly different needs. Is this something you’d consider adding to the app??

I LOVE this app! I’ve got 30+ houseplants of all kinds and it can sometime be a headache to remember when one needs to be watered. Not only does this app remind you but it lets you assign a picture to the plant so in case you forget the name of the plant (or someone is housesitting and is unfamiliar) it’s easy to find the plant you’re looking for among your collection. I check this app every day and it’s fun to show off my collection with my green thumbed friends. This is definitely an asset!
With that said, my criticism lies in two areas: there is no option to water early. I have a few plants that always need to be watered a day or two earlier than recommended and there is no way to record that. The closest option is to go ahead and water then choose the option to ‘snooze’ but that will throw off the watering record. My second criticism is that the selection of plants is somewhat limited. Several of my succulents which I know the species aren’t in the Planta catalogue. I’d love an option to add to the database (perhaps this is available in the premium version but I’m against paywall restrictions so hopefully this isn’t the case).

title: Great app, needs more flexibility
review: I recently started using this app again after I saw it got an update, but unfortunately there are a lot of features I think this app still needs. There’s no option to edit your plants needs, which can be frustrating when you disagree with planta’s watering recommendations, or if you definitely have a plant that needs regular cleaning (I have a dusty house) but planta’s rules for that plant have it so the plant never needs cleaning. There’s also only one option for fertilizer not added with watering, which is a 3 month stick. I use a 6 month soil mix in, so again it would be great if there were more options. It’s also weird how when I add a new plant, I answer all the questions the app prompts, but then the app lets me know that plant information is still missing, so I need to go back in and add more. Just let me add it all at once. I also wish there was more flexibility, some of my plants have both windows and grow lights, and also how much light a grow light gives is dependent on the strength of the bulb and the distance from the bulb, but planta lets me add in time that the grow light is on. This app has a lot of promise and is probably totally adequate for the casual plant owner, I just really wish it was more useful for those of us that are a little more crazy about our many plants.

title: Started out great, each update makes things worse :/
review:
I got this app over a year ago when I really started getting into plants. I researched a bunch of apps, tried a few out, and like Planta the best. However since then, a number of updates have made it much less easy to use or messed things up. Now that they finally got rid of the bug where it gets stuck and doesn’t mark a plant watered when you check it (really fun to close the app each time I watered one of my 180+ plants 😩), new problems arise!

This seems like an intended change, though I’m not sure why - they got rid of the alphabet on the right side, so you can’t just click on a letter and go to it, you have to scroll and scroll and scroll to get to it. Why on earth would you get rid of that?? Of course to make it worse, there is an unintended bug to go along with it - the Search function on your plant list doesn’t work anymore. So literally the only way you have to find a certain plant is to SCROLL and scroll and scroll forever. Who has time for that? I got an app to make my hobby easier, not harder. And I intended to get the premium version once I got more into plants/felt like I needed it….although I do need it, I haven’t gotten it because there is always some issue. If the basic features don’t work/are taken away, I’m not going to pay for a premium version. Get it together.

title: Amazing But....
review:
This app is amazing and works well. I have been watering my plants every time I get a notification. I am still a new ish plant owner. Because I have only recently gotten into plants. I personally think that the plant scanner should be free. Now hear me out. I can not afford to pay for Premium. And a lot of the plants (succulents) I buy do not have the name of it on the tag. For instance one of the succulents I bought from a store was just called “succulent in a tin”. I was unable to identify the plant and because I am unable to afford Premium I could not find out the name. Thus resulting in me having to go under “cacti and succulents” and scrolls for like 2 and a half hours before I was able to find the correct name of the succulent bought.

You are also ( from my knowledge) unable to change the main picture of your plant. When the plants grows more or I move it or I repot it I would like to be able to change to main picture of the plant. For example, I just recently repoted my ivy and was unable to change the photo that is showed when I need to water the plant. But I am only able to add pictures to the “add details” spot after watering and it does not update  the main photo. 

Overall these are my only problems. And the app is amazing other wise. I hope this was able to help someone. 🌿🌿

title: Great app for keeping your plants healthy!
review:
I’ve been using Planta for just over 4 months now as a premium user and I love it. It helps me keep my plants organized and healthy. While I am a relatively new plant “parent”, and I rely on it to help me know when to water, fertilize, and generally care for all of my plants (35!), I know that I still have to trust my own instincts and that every plant is different. That’s why I enjoy the features Planta has in place to make sure you care for your plants in ways that work for you. I enjoy all the features, including the plant health tracker, and access to a plant doctor bot for plants that are in trouble. For the most part all of my plants are thriving. 

That being said, I would ask for Planta to think about adding a vacation mode feature into the app that lets you switch your schedules for the amount of time you will be away. Not all of us have people who will look after our plants while we are away, and it would be nice to be able to modify the watering schedule without having to snooze plants every 2 days until you get back. Also a tips section regarding how to prepare your plants for your vacation would be super nice, too. Maybe also a calendar view for upcoming activity would be a nice future add, too. 😊

title: Latest update has created a nearly unusable app
review:
The app used to work wonderfully. But I would honestly recommend passing on it until they implement some fixes. I’m not sure if it was the latest update, but suddenly I have a very laggy, buggy app with no way to mark plants as watered (if you happen to deter from their schedule). It’s actually created a lot of confusion and I have a dozen or so plants that are completely out of whack with the app not properly recording data. 

Aside from that, the app no longer wants to mark any task as complete without a fight.  I have 50+ plants, so this can mean a lot of tasks in one day. It freezes on the loading screen when you click the check mark and in most cases, I’m having to force close the app just to get off that screen. Sometimes the task is recorded, sometimes it’s not. If it’s not, you click the check mark again and it gives you a red error (presumably it did record the task just not anywhere you can see), and then it’ll finally show it as complete on your end. This is a lot of added steps towards the main function of this app. It’s supposed to make things more convenient and easy to track and right now, I do not feel it is living up to that.

Again, I used to LOVE this app and if they can turn these more recent issues around, I would recommend it. I just feel any newcomers will find it very frustrating in its current state.

title: Super helpful app through winter…
review:
I have had the Planta app for probably 6 -8 months at this point. Through the winter, I think it was fabulous and pretty on point with watering schedules so I mostly didn’t have to think twice about it and would just water my plants when it told me to. This is a big deal for me as someone who loves plants but at this point in my plant journey I would say I am a beginner and definitely worry about over or under watering. But, now that we have gotten into summer I feel like the accuracy of telling me when to water is completely off. It wants me to water individual plants every couple of days and they are always still wet when I check them. I know the weather has changed, but these are indoor plants, they are not out baking in 90 degree weather so their watering schedule for the summer probably really should have only shifted to just slightly more frequently than they were being watered in the winter. At this point I feel like I cannot trust the watering schedule in the app and so I am probably going to have to look at other options. Please please please give your summer watering schedule a look and see if there are other factors that should be worked into the formula to make it more accurate! 

Updated July 21 - app is now duplicating my plants so I have multiples of the same plant, same picture and everything but the duplicates have different watering schedule info. Took a risk and deleted one of the duplicates of a new plant so that I wouldn’t lose history if it deleted both…..yep it deleted both. This app was fantastic now it is definitely starting to stress me out!

title: Some bugs that need fixing
review:
Overall, I think this app is great! I paid for the annual subscription. As a plant novice, the watering/fertilizing/misting schedule has, if anything, helped me to become more familiar with my plants. There a few things I think could use some improvement.

-Sometimes, based on the “info” portion for each plant, the app will say for example “water every 6th day in September”. However I would notice that I wouldn’t get a notification to water that plant even after 6 days have passed
-fertilizing/watering schedule. The app will notify you when it’s time to fertilize your plant, which must be done with a watering. However, once you have performed and checked off the task for fertilizing, you then have to add an extra task that you’ve watered the plant. If not, the app will think that perhaps you haven’t watered since the last check-off, and will then remind to water at a sooner than necessary date, which may lead to overwatering. So typically, whenever there is a reminder to fertilize and no reminder on the same day to water, I’ll have to go to the plant profile and determine if I should snooze the fertilize task, or both water and fertilize that day. Or perhaps the main issue is that the app will remind to fertilize when it’s not even time for a watering. It can get confusing, but I’ve found my way around it.

title: Needs to be improved
review: One thing that doesn’t make sense is the fact that you can’t personalize the dates for when it notifies you to water your plants. The day you download the add is the automatic day all your plants need to be watered. What if I had watered my plant before I downloaded the app? Also some of my plants don’t need to be watered yet but I continue to get notifications that I have tasks that are late. Also I gave one of my plants extra water and I wasn’t able to track it because the app considered it to early so the option wasn’t even given to document it. Also it sets automatic days you have to water your plant. For example every 9 days you have to water your monstera but this doesn’t consider the size of the plant. A bigger plant has different watering needs then a smaller plant of the same kind. I do like the plant helper feature that helps you diagnose what’s wrong with your plant. I also like how it has a lot of information about a wide variety of plants and includes pictures. Another think I forgot is the app is demanding me to repot my plant but why?? There is no reason to so why am I getting the notification to do it? All the information I gave was that my plant was in a plastic pot in a medium lit room. What could have indicated I needed to repot my plant from that information given? The light meter feature was also helpful might I add. I was a premium member for about 4 weeks but now I think I’m switching to another app.

title: Not great for succulents
review: This app seems to be really good for some plants, but it usually misidentifies any succulent or cactus. Most of my succulents, even one that’s a totally different color and shape, come up as Mexican Snowball echeveria, which they are obviously not. It did just fine identifying peace lily, spider plant, ZZ plant, corn plant, pothos, philodendron, etc. so it seems to be an issue just with the succulents, which is frustrating for me because they comprise the majority of my collection. I wish there was an option to put in past information. Sometimes I’m lazy or I don’t remember to put the information till a day or two later, but the best I can do is to mark it watered today. I’d prefer if I could chose to put in more accurate information. The schedule the app suggests doesn’t usually end up working for my plants. I put all there information in as accurately as possible, but there were still lots of days that one plant starts drooping or another has completely dry soil long before the recommended watering day. It would be kind of nice if the app could keep track of the frequency and maybe adjust itself to better match my regular watering schedule. It’s possible that I need to manipulate the data even more, though. One thing I do appreciate is the reminders to mist. I didn’t realize certain plants needed misting or how often to do it. Hopefully, that will be one more thing to help the tropical plants thrive in the dry climate here. The fact that it isn’t great for succulents is the biggest dealbreaker for me. I’m not sure if I will want to renew my subscription when the time comes.

title: 4 stars
review:
Edit:  I bought the subscription after they offered it at a big discount to start. They still don't have greenhouses or starting with seeds and it seems to have me over water my plants a bit during the winter but they do have grow lights now. The free version was good to get me started but the subscription is even better now that I have more plants. It tells me when to water, mist, clean the leaves so the plant can photosynthesize better, fertilize, and repot.  The app has a light meter that will help tell you where the light is better for different types of plants. If you turn your phone looking out a window and it says partly shady then you know you shouldn't put a plant that needs full sun there. And only if you have a subscription if your plant has a problem and the AI can't figure it out then you can contact a person and they will run through the steps with you to help you figure out what the issue is. 
The newest updates have added plants in the ground, plant sitters, family members to help keep your plants happy, and groups to join (both general and specific) to ask questions, to help others and answer questions, to post pictures, and to gloat.

I really like this app. I haven’t paid for the premium subscription yet because there can be some improvement. One of my biggest issues is that it doesn’t have plants starting out as a seed. I like to start a lot of my own plants from seeds. Greenhouse is another. I have a very small greenhouse because I live in the middle of the desert. I am very limited on the plants I can grow outside because the heat just roasts them most of the year. And grow lights for work great getting plants started from seeds. Those are just my top three improvements I would like to see done before I get the subscription or make this a 5-star rating.

title: Good concept, but needs work
review:
I almost don’t want to recommend any new plant owners use this app, with the fixed watering schedule without knowing your location and tracking your local weather, you may get your plants killed with this app.
I’ve been using the app for one month now. I’m not an expert on plants, but I have about 20 indoor and outdoor plants that lives over 5+ years. 
A healthy plant requires more than just watering, it also depends on lighting, and local weather. Even in the same house, you may experienced a plant grows different on a different location of the house. 
For Planta’s free plant, it only offers FIXED watering dates, which you can’t even make personalization changes. Does paid version fix this problem? It didn’t say—this, the marketing team did a bad job on promoting the paid version. With the fixed schedule, for my tomato I bought in March, it’s recommending to water every 3 days, until today, May 7, it still says the same thing. But I live in California and today the highest temperature is above 90, you basically have to water tomato everyday otherwise it’s gonna die. Same with my indoor plants. One plant I’ve been watering it once a week for years, then Planta suggests to water it every two weeks. I decided to give it a try, and going to stop this suggestion as I see the plant leaves gotten bad. 
I’m currently debating on deleting this app, as I don’t see its being actually helpful.

title: Very Interested…But
review: I refuse to use Apple Pay Wallet or PayPal due to painful identity theft. I was willing to submit my one credit card for payment. It was not accepted but rather recommended the aforementioned subscription & payments option. Nope! As much I would enjoy this. I can find other resources. Maybe not as fancy or as detailed, but not as risky either. The App creators should not be limited to Apple’s Monopoly on payment methods. You are losing subscribers while Apple makes money on the device, your software and rejecting any payment option that won’t contribute to their monopoly. As soon as my Apple phone is extinct, as is my iMac and iPad, I’m done with Apple. There is absolutely nothing wrong with our other products EXCEPT Apple will not updated the operating system. We are expected to purchase simply because Apple refuses to update older models. HA! Not happening. We have a cheap laptop & are living fine without our iPads. Your company should be investigated for unfair business practices and illegal monopoly. Not that I care. I’m a professional trouble shooter. I can work around your greedy (liberal) money grabbing lack of decency. Just watch! Tired of your B.S. and your in-your-face politics. All about it green energy while you bury perfectly good computers, etc. because you choose the almighty dollar over the environment. Climate change is about making money. Planta developers suffer because you want me to use your payment scheme. Disgusting!!

title: Gets The Job Done Great
review:
This is perfect for what I wanted- reminders to water the plants and info on how to care for them. I have just a couple things that could be better. 
First, if the free version had just a bit more than watering- at least the plant doctor, maybe- that’s be fantastic. I only have the free version, and I have wished several times for the plant doctor, but not often enough to buy a membership. Maybe a limited use- you get to use the plant doctor twice a month or something. That’d be totally awesome, and I’d honestly give the app a 5 star rating if it did that. But, I get that the app people have to make money somehow. 
Second, it would be nice if you could customize the sites a tad more- particularly the temperature. I would like to have a site for my greenhouse. And a brief description of the difference between each site- bedroom and kitchen and all- would be nice, if there even is a difference.
Finally, if this app could be expanded to outdoor gardening I would instantly rate 5 stars and probably recommend to everyone. I imagine that’d take awhile to design though. Maybe make a sister app? 
Anyway, there are several things that could make this app fantastic, but it is already very good. I like it very much, and will continue to use it.

title: This is my second review, and…
review: This app is great! This is my second review, I’ve run into a couple problems, but nothing too big. First- I think Dr Planta should be open to everyone. Because if you are getting Planta, there is a good chance it’s because your plants are sick or dying. Second- my succulents are sharing pots with others. For example, a have a two inch succulent in a 8 inch pot ( from side to side over the top ) sharing with other plants. However, the app does not know it is sharing its pot, and it may be giving me false information. Me and my succulents are doing good, but this may be a problem in the future. Third- this is just for succulents, but whenever you take a leaf off of a thick-leaved succulent, you can put in in sun and a new plant will grow from the leaf. This is called propagation, and this should be an option to grow your plants in the app. Like, say, and option to watch over your propagation plants, care, facts, and more. It’s just for succulents of course, though. Otherwise, the app is amazing, and you did an amazing job!! I’m usually really critical on plant apps ( I just love my succulents ) so just want you guys to know you did an amazing job!!!!!

title: Not sure I can really trust Planta…🤔
review:
I have been using Planta for a good while now & overall ❤️ the concept of having an app keep me on track w/ taking care of my plants as my collection grew. I’ve shared with friends how much I love the Planta app! However, over the time Ive been using it, I have definitely lost some plants & I believe there’s a likelihood that it’s bcz of the bugs in planta - like not updating schedules when changes are made by the app user. If I decide to skip an action such as watering cz it appears my plant doesn’t need to be watered yet, I’m no longer confident that the app actually recalculates when the plant will need to be watered or updates based on my change. Sometimes it feels like I’m watering & fertilizing so often that it’s just not making sense & I think that’s due to that issue.
The other big concern I have with planta is that when I have had a sick plant, I found the Dr. Plants advice to be so contradictory that I was just left not knowing what the heck to do.  It’s just not helpful to be told 2 different issues on the opposite end of the spectrum are causing your plant to be sick ( I.e. over/under watering for example).  Every time I go through the process of using Dr. Planta I come away feeling more confused than  when I started
but frankly, I often find the same to be true of Internet advice about plants. 
I recently moved a plant from soil to water & Planta definitely isn’t reading that, bcz it continues to offer a watering schedule. 
Overall, I would say that when I chose to pay for the app, I wanted something that would do a lot of the thinking for me, and I could trust that it was giving me the proper advice. I now think that expectation was  unrealistic.

title: I Love This App!
review: Planta is almost perfect at what it does—I can see my whole indoor garden by room, I can set room conditions to help dictate an automatic care schedule, it reminds me who needs what and when… The thing is I use it to make plant care easier given the number of houseplants I have and one small tweak would make it much better at this: let the user select the number of days (or weeks) to snooze a task. That’s it. Since I have so many plants, having to choose 2 days for a plant I know I don’t need to touch again for a month makes the whole app useless at reducing work required because now I have 20 snoozed plants popping up in 2 days. There is an alternative option to “skip until next time” but again that too would be better with selectable numbers as I have no idea what next time is from that prompt. Even the forecasted care schedule should be editable. Maybe Planta is suggesting fertilizing next week and I want to schedule it for next month instead or maybe it’s forecasting a repotting and I want to do it sooner or never based on observing the plant. This way when I get a task or upcoming task, it’d have so much more value. These seem like easy changes from a user perspective that would be fantastic.

title: Great app, needs minor improvements
review:
Edit: Thank you for pointing out these features! I have one suggestion for future updates: please add a basic chart for how much to water based on pot size. That would be helpful to avoid under or over watering.  

Useful for keeping track of watering/fertilizing houseplants under ideal circumstances, but isn’t easy to adjust schedules when conditions are less than ideal. We’ve had unseasonably high temperatures which meant many of my plants, especially the ones in direct sun, needed more water, more often. I wanted to add an unscheduled watering for a few of plants but there is no way to do that without putting each of them on a fully customized permanent schedule. There should be an option to document that a plant was watered outside of the day recommended by the app. Also, the location feature is not very helpful. I get warnings from the app that a specific room is not appropriate, but the light meter readings any room will vary dramatically if you move a few inches up or down, or to the left or right. But the location is saved with only one set recommendation for the whole space. Not very helpful.

title: Great app! But…
review: First, I really do like this app. It’s probably helped keep my plants alive longer than they would’ve lived without me using Planta. So thank you for that. But seriously, whose idea was it to change the home screen format? To something clearly worse, aesthetically and intuitively. It makes zero sense to have a huge box for every plant that needs to be watered or fertilized in the today view. It was much better when there was one box for every plant that needed to be watered. All plants clear in sight with little to no scrolling, check boxes to complete each one, and importantly, for those with many plants, a complete all tasks option. Then a separate one for plants being fertilized. Now, each plant has its own huge box, so it’s more cluttered, ugly, requires more scrolling, and generally takes more time because it’s less clear cut than before. Please come up with something better, or at least go back to what it was before. Seriously, it’s head scratching how this even came to be. Everything else is great. Tho I don’t use the marketplace or social functions at all. I purely use it to keep my plants alive.

title: Not for desert-dwellers
review:
So admittedly I’m new at plants, but even with the location classification, the watering schedule is way off. I’m from Phoenix, and the app told me to water a dracaena once a month... lol. I left for a week and the soil was bone-dry. It’s too bad- the app is beautifully done. I’ll try setting my own schedules, but that seems like it defeats the purpose of the app.

ETA: I triple-checked my inputs. 9b, dry air, draft, correct temp, partial sun, and nursery pot. Literally the exact plant type from the sign. And we’re talking bone-dry, crispy-tips, soil-comes-out-in-one-brick level. I don’t think there’s any dracaena that wants to be that dry for 20 days, especially one that likes humidity (I should add that it has its own humidifier that’s on a daily timer). I also asked around last time I was at the nursery, and they said 10-14 days. I’ve been taking moisture readings daily and in its current location, the soil from the nursery dries completely in 6 days. I am having similar results with my other plants, as well, but most of them are desert plants who aren’t as dramatic about moisture as the dracaena is. If I missed something, please let me know.

Again, it’s an awesome app and I have no doubt it works perfectly for the majority of people. If I had 50 bucks to just mess around with pro, maybe it would work better.  The free version’s recommendations just aren’t gonna work for me.

title: One Addition I Think Should Be Added, Considering The Price!
review: I downloaded this after seeing it in the Apple store, but upon seeing the price for a year, and no permanent price, for instance, I was rather dismayed to discover that there wasn’t a list of the current plants that could be shown to us with their photos and common and scientific names, before we purchase this app for any length of time or of the premium plan! I happen to be a multi year customer of two major nurseries back east, in Connecticut and in Florida, and they have a vast selection of the rarest tropical plants and tropical flowers and tropical fruit, of anywhere in the country, and possibly in the entire world including Australia! Before I would purchase this, I would want to have communications with this developer and give them the names of those nurseries and await their response, and know that they do have all of the needed information first! I am not about to pay down $36, and then find it won’t be of little or any use to me! But I think they give us too little to make any real determination about whether we want his app or not, and rather force us into paying for this before we have any real idea of how much good or not, it would do us in attending to our plants correctly, considering the vast array of plants that are out there! It’s much easier to get information about plants that grow in this United States, but not from outside of our borders!

title: So easy and functional.
review: I have about 30 plants of all kinds in my house. I needed a plant management system to help me. I have tried three systems with just five plants each to see which system had the most features and also was easy to use. I used the premium feature that has to be paid for on two of the apps. After two weeks of kicking the tires on each one, I found Planta to have the most features right at the place where you need them.  Here is an example- the plant watering schedule will list all the plants that need watering that day with a picture you provided or the one out of their library. Let’s say your plant does not need watering that day and you want more info on the watering requirements of that plant. Just click on plant picture and then all the plant info appears. It presents this cool chart for each plant showing the water requirements by month so you can adjust your watering requirements. So in the warm period (Feb-Octin your plant hardiness zone) you can set the watering schedule you need to do. Then you can set a different watering schedule for that plant in the cold period. Pretty cool and so easy. I am still trying out all the other features. Great app.

title: Good app, but could use some changes.
review:
Great concept, and really cool for the plants it has support for. However, there are a lot of plants (especially California native plants!) that don’t have any support. There should be an option to add your own plants in and put in the associated watering schedule, much like the current “custom care” setting. That way, people who know their plants can still have the benefits of having all their plant lists in one place. Also, it is odd to me that the scientific names of the plants are so hidden. Most serious plant growers are familiar with scientific names more so than common names, and it’s a little frustrating when search results come in sorted by common name  with only the genus visible (sometime). When i tried to find a plant that the app did not support i tried to search the genus but the results were muddled by the common names. So in summary: this app would be even better if users can add their own plants in (possibly contributing to plantas database of plant knowledge; making it easier on devs to add new plant support), and if common names were less emphasized than scientific names. 

Update: thanks for the response! Changed my rating to 5 stars.

title: I’d give 10 stars if I could!!!
review:
I am not one to EVER write a review for anything but I am such a firm believer in this app that I feel obligated to. I recently moved into my own apartment and have always appreciated plants but decided I wanted to take it to the next level and have many throughout my home, unfortunately I knew nothing about caring for plants and they’d often times die. Since I have got this app my plants have not only been flourishing but two of my plants have come back from the dead - seriously!!! 
My striped Calathea for example was so unhappy, literally brown sticks that were about to be thrown away but I decided to try this app before letting it go and sure enough after just a couple short weeks I saw life! My plant now has four beautiful, healthy leaves growing and my family seriously doesn’t believe I didn’t just go to the store and replace it because it seemed like there was no hope - but there was - Planta!!! 

This isn’t fake, I’m not being paid, I’m just so passionate and tell everyone how amazing this app is because it has saved my plants and makes my space look amazing and healthy!!

title: Hands down the best plant app
review: I have around 40 houseplants and this has been a god send. I’ve tried over 20 apps, and this blows them all out the water. The plant recognition function is hands down the most impressive. It was even able to identify my dead African Marigolds from JUST the shriveled up stem. That’s a miracle and far better than others that were unable to detect even some basic, healthy plants. I love how it auto sets your watering schedule based on your location and environment (instead of manually having to add it). The only function I find lacking is the Doctor function. It is kind of basic and stops after a few prompts. If there was an option to take a picture of your sick plant and have the Doctor tell you what was wrong based on that, then this will make this app go above and beyond. For example, something that would identify pest types by a picture you take in the same way it detects the plant type….and have it able to detect what is wrong with the leaves or branches. It should be easy for the app to see that a succulent plant is over watered based on it being swollen and yellowish.

title: Excellent
review:
SUGGESTION: please please please, create a Greenhouse option , where the variables are the same .  Thank you! 
UPDATE: OMG- the weather app…. thank you - thank you !! It even routs to my watch so no updates are missed. Incredible work. Also, discovered that Dr. Planta is generic and not plant specific , hopefully the data base grows and becomes more customizable. PRO- -company is incredibly responsive and seem to take feedback seriously. You can see their replies to customers feedback under the review section -more user friendly than many other apps I’v tried -the plant recognition is impressive and it was able to id. all but one of my plants. (water jasmine) -the information given is detailed and i’m excited to take progress pictures -It helps you find the most suitable place in your home via its light detector to place your plant to thrive -It reminds you daily of plant tasks. This can be annoying for some but, I’m forgetful and the reminder is appreciated. -I didn’t realize that I had 22 plants, inputting the information can be a little lengthy if you have a lot of plants as I did, but the investment seems to be worth it for the information alone. -It provides feedback on wether or not your plant is conducive to the zone that you live in to grow successfully. This app is super useful when you have more than 5 plants that range from tropical, to vegetables, to bonsais, to succulents. GROWS: -It would be incredible to have the app sync with the weather and alert when plants need to come in. (hail, cold front, high winds) to help alter water schedules as a result- low humidity water more, high =less, cold front =no water , etc.. SO- the free subscription is great but the app really shines when you upgrade. It’s affordable,( 3$/month,sacrifice a Starbucks and support the developers instead ) so worth it !

title: Best plant app💐🌷
review: If you are looking for an app so you can rihtly take care of your plants without them dying, this is the one. I have had plenty of plants that have died before this app, and since then, Planta has been supporting me with so many ideas to help my plants grow. Planta holds so many species of plants, there would be no way your plant wasnt on the list. It gives you a doctor for when your plant is sick, it gives you suggestions, it gives you groups you can talk to to make sure your plants is havin the time of its life. There are great watering schedules, fertilizer, pruning, etc reminders to help your plants thrive! The Planta subscription is also cheap, yet so helpful with so much important information. You wont lose a buck when I tell you that this app is the greatest plant app you would ever have seen. Grow your plants outdoor or indoor, Planta will always give you everything you need to keep all of your plants happy as they grow. If your plant dies, no worries, you can bring it back in days with help from Dr. Planta! Take this review as a welcome from Planta and the amazing things they hold!

title: 1 year of use, countless plants saved!
review:
I couldn’t understand how I was killing so many plants until this app. Since getting this app a little over a year ago, I’ve only lost a handful of plants, and I think that’s below average. Plants bite the dust sometimes no matter what we do. But this app taught me how and when to use fertilizer, when to water and how, and how much light is too much or too little. It’s so mindless, it’s perfect. Open the app, see what needs what, do that, done. No puzzling out what to do. 

I get the sense this app is a labor of love for the developers, and I have seen improvements throughout the year. There are still some improvements to be made, but those can only be made by more money coming in. I’d absolutely recommend this app to anyone with plants, and already have. It is such a steal to have this for $35 per year. Probably saved around $200 by not killing plants and having to buy new ones! Even started propagating plants which has saved even more money. In the future it would be a really cool addition to have info on how to propagate each plant!

title: Too good to be true
review: I think at the end of the day this concept might be a little bit too good to be true. Asking technology to inform us about nature is really counterintuitive when I think about it I should probably be giving myself the two star review in trusting tech to influence my plant care. I downloaded this app and purchased a subscription out of curiosity and convenience. Generally I can take care of plants no problem having come from a long line of farmers and ranchers. Unfortunately, however, after following this apps advice to the letter, my body count has risen to three separate tropical house plants in the matter of months (living in a tropical climate mind you). I experimented in stopping following planta’s advice and purchasing the exact house plants that I killed and they are thriving now. I’m not claiming to be an expert or knowing better than planta at all. But I am claiming that advice from the app caused me to overwater and kill 2 plants ($60 in value). In conclusion (if you’ve gotten this far) I don’t have any ill will towards this company nor do I think that they have bad intentions, but I would not trust their advice to a fault and I would recommend following your best judgment if you’ve ever been able to keep a plant alive by yourself.

title: Not as good as it was
review: After using this app for several months, my opinion of it has fallen significantly. It started out great, but this last update just it not for me. The “beta” version of the app that helps you identify problems you may be having with your plants is absolutely terrible because if you do not already know what the problem is then you’re clueless on how to proceed with the questions it asks. The previous method was to show pictures and ask you to identify what was closest to your issue and it was super easy and step by step. Furthermore, the app has slowed so much that I no longer have the patience for it. When you tap on the icon to complete a task, such as watering, it takes at least 45 seconds of spinning wheel to update. Then it will auto refresh to the top of your list, causing you to have to scroll all the way back down to where you where. Based on these minor annoyances and the fact that I was unable to contact support through their channels, I am leaving my review here and canceling my subscription.

title: Could be improved
review:
I’m a paid member, and I absolutely love this app. It keeps me on track when the number of plants I have to take care of is overwhelming. It’s beautiful and gives great information on each plant. The reason for 3 stars is because I think there are so many ways it could be improved. Namely, more customizations and better care info. 

I wish I could give my pilea plant a custom task like “rotate once every three days” or something. Or I could choose which image I want as the main picture for my plant while still adding more pictures in its personal album. I wish the app included the size of the pot in how often we need to water, because my smaller pots need water much more often than my larger ones too. I also wished the care instructions were more in depth. Each plant is given the same categories of care, but as plant owners know, some plants have very specific care needs. It would be great if each plant had its own small blurb at the end written by someone at the planta team which felt more personal. These suggestions are just to name a few. 

I hope with more and more updates we start to see an app with better functionality while still keep its clean and easy-to-use look.

title: Needs a vacation algorithm
review: I love this app! Been a paid subscriber for over 2 years now and I can 100% say there is no other app better than this for tracking your plants. That being said, with the number of plants I have it can get overwhelming sometimes when the daily tasks start to add up. I simply don’t have time to do all the tasks needed every single day. I’m hoping the developers could introduce an algorithm that could possibly consolidate a week’s tasks down to a few days, for example if I want to go on vacation for a long 4-day weekend, I could put this in and it will tell me what to do to prepare and what to do when I get back. Or if I don’t have daily time I can dedicate to plant care, I can configure settings to permanently consolidate my tasks down to a selection of days I choose, instead of every day. Then Planta could advise if this is enough days, or if I have plants that need daily care it could warn about that too. Seems like a good idea. Anyways, Planta is still the best! 5 stars!

title: Happy but hoping for a crucial improvement
review: I am so grateful a coworker told me about Planta. It makes my life so much easier! They continue to update it as well with new improvements. I haven’t ran into any issues with identifying or finding a houseplant so their database of plants and plant knowledge must be extensive, even for rarer houseplants. The biggest complaint I have is the progress reminder update and water reminder update are the SAME look/color! This might not seem like a big deal but when you glance at 6 of your plants in a row all orange with a notification to water and there is one that follows that says progress but also looks the exact same my mind naturally sees this as another plant that needs to be watered. It does say Progress instead of Water but because the notification is the same look/color next to the plant on numerous occasions now I’ve accidentally overwatered my plants. This small error as killed a few of my plants. I doubt I am the only person who has done this. Please update this feature and make it so the Progress update does not look so similar to the Water update. It would make the app more useful and my plants happier!

title: Not enough info
review:
I’ve found that there are several plants that aren’t available, and there are no options for choosing which varieties of plants. For example, bush varieties vs pole varieties, which need different care. There’s also no info about germination. The subscription is expensive considering there are countless websites online that can give you all of the information provided in this app. Without forking out the extra money for the premium service, this app is almost useless. Every time I saw something that might be useful, I was met with more and more asking for my money. 

This is a great concept and I was excited to have a central place to keep my plant care organized and to get help when I need it as a beginner/moderate plant parent. But plant care alone being costly as it is, I have no desire to spend money on a subscription service for information that I can access with a quick google search. If it were a one time purchase I’d be much more willing to give this app a chance but I can’t justify spending several dollars a month. 

TLDR: it’s a good concept and might be nice for a busy person with a high number of plants, but is too expensive to be useful, and does not have much variety for plant types.

title: Almost love this!
review: This app is so close to a 4-star in my book, but it could be a 5-star app. I’m a Planta user and pay for the membership because it is worth it compared to other apps like this. The app is nice! It allows you to find out what any unknown new plant friends you brought in. It helps you determine the best place to put your plants. It even reminds you when to water, mist, and fertilize. However, you only have access to some of these functions as a paying member. I think it would be nice to allow these functions for free but offer paying members access to online plant help through the app for beginners to work one on one and maybe open forums for users to chat when help isn’t available? Also, I feel like there are fewer “homesteader” plant options available, which leads me to having to turn to other sources. I think that especially right now, the app would benefit from that. Many people are starting to grow their own foods at home right now. Also it would be cool to see how-to content about care for each plant. You could have people submit videos to reach out to the public about this. Taking care of my plants has been one of the things getting me through this!

title: Planta Saved My Plants!
review:
I LOVE PLANTA! I have 40+ plants and this app has changed my life and the lives of my plants! I killed so many of my plants before I found Planta! I’ve tried a few apps, and while some are pretty good, Planta blows them away. Enough notifications that I know what I need to do, but not too many to be annoying. Fantastic watering and care instructions that have made my plants go from dying to flourishing in very little time. The app just makes sense, the instructions and articles are informative and helpful, and the search function has more varieties than I could have ever hoped for. 
The free, no-subscription option is great! I never ran into a limit of plants, and My mother-in-law says I have too many 😂 You can get advice about if the plant you’re looking at will do ok in the space and time you have. You get spot-on watering schedules for the specific plant based on time of year, where you are in the world, and what the particular plant needs. You can take advantage of progress updates where you can track growth and whether you’re seeing a trend of a problem. And you have articles that give more information on what’s the best way to water your plant (top, bottom, soaking, etc). I’ve become a far better plant caretaker simply because of the free benefits. 
However the Pro subscription is a heaven-sent miracle worker. Schedules for misting, fertilization, pruning, repotting, cleaning, and more! And the same impressive level of education and personalization for each and every task as I saw with just the watering. The plant identifier that uses the camera is far more accurate than anything else I’ve tried. And while I haven’t used it that much, Dr. Planta seems like a valuable asset. 
I tell anyone that stands still for too long to get this app. Anyone who’s just learning how to take care of plants, anyone who’s trying to save dying plants, anyone who feels like they’re fairly competent with their plants. Everyone should get Planta!

title: My plants LOVE Planta!!
review:
I absolutely love this app! It really helps me take better care of my 50+ plants. Before Planta, I was watering most of my plants on the same schedule and while they were still alive, they weren’t thriving. After using Planta for a couple of months, and each plant being on its own schedule, I have noticed a HUGE difference in my plants and how much healthier and happier they look. 

I am, however, not a fan of the newest update. Managing the daily tasks is confusing.  When I checked this morning, before the new update was pushed to my phone, it said I only had 3 tasks but when I just checked it now, it says I have 35 but doesn’t give the snooze or complete option next to each plant (like it did before). Maybe I’m not looking at it right and it could be user error. I’m gonna have to reacquaint myself with the app to figure it out. 

But even with that update, I still recommend this app to all my plant friends. Definitely worth the price of the premium option!

title: Amazing app! Want more social options
review:
I love planta so much and it has been great for me as i’ve gotten deeper into the rabbit hole of plant ownership! super convenient for both me and to give to people plant sitting for me to give them a guideline of when to water

One thing I think would be fun to add is more of a social side to the app? many of my friends are also into plants and i think it would be cool to be able to browse their collections or to be able to send each other planta you think the other person would like! also to be able to transfer plants between accounts if you give a plant to a friend and then you can watch it’s progress on your friends page instead of just completely deleting it from your library. ooh or a little “cutting/propagates family tree” from the og plant to all of the new babies. 

I realize adding social is probably a huge endeavor so i don’t see it happening soon but just thought it could be a cool direction for the app to go eventually!

title: Amazing App, 1 Suggestion
review: I have finally upgraded my account to Premium and am loving it even more now. However, I do see one inconvenient thing regarding the fertilizer options. I believe another user also brought this up. When you add a plant it asks how you want to fertilize it.. I clicked “slow release sticks” for some of my plants but have started using the little pump bottles by Miracle Gro for both succulents and indoor plants instead. I cannot change this as a setting for my plants, and do not want to go back in and re-add them just to update the fertilizer settings. Is this a feature that can be added to an future update? The fertilizer schedule isn’t accurate now since I would most likely be using the pump fertilizer more frequently than the slow release sticks.  Other than this feature that I wish could be changed, this is an extremely helpful and thorough app, and I even use it in the classroom with my students for the plants they have brought in!

title: Very useful app, with a few limitations
review:
- I love having a list of plants to check on for watering each day, as well as a record of when I last watered. I can't imagine having this many plants without it
- the watering predictions have been relatively accurate for most of my plants
- I love having an organized collection of photos and records for each plant

Missing features

- no orchid pot in pot type. It dries much faster than other plastic pots
- every time you water "early" you get a warning about over watering. I wish I could turn these off. The worst part is it still reminds you even if you have snoozed watering once or multiple times and are watering days later than planta originally recommended 
- I wish there was a an option in between a custom schedule and the planta recommendation. I like how the planta recommendations adjust for time of year, but I have some plants that consistently need to be watered sooner than the schedule suggests. I wish we could keep monthly adjustments, but indicate "a little sooner" or "a little later" 
- the light options are pretty lacking. Since full sun is 8+ hours of light, my unobstructed south facing windows that get 6 hours of direct midday sun and my obstructed East facing window that gets 1 hour of morning sun both count as "partial sun" to the app, even though they are extremely different
- it would be nice if we could set indoor temperatures. In the summer my house was quite warm, which I suspect is why my plants needed more frequent watering than planta expected

title: App is Limited
review: The app is good for everyday use if you pay for premium, I’m just disappointed in the options in learning about weather your lil green dude is in a good place, EX. I have a store bought monstera adanonsii and it came in water (hydroponically).  I can’t find anything on here whether or not it’s ok or not or even how to care for it in a situation I have. This app is good for soil keepers and that’s about it. Glad I didn’t get premium to end up with info that didn’t need. I just want an informative app that allows me to run scheduling for my plants. Now granted it does that but just very cut and dry and limited in options. And even if my plant isn’t meant for hydroponic growing there isn’t a feature to advise me about it. Limited care and is just not as informative as it’s made to seem being a creators choice or whatever it is. Now granted they did have that option I hope that I could at least run a weeks worth at minimum of premium care for a plant before I have to pay. I just think this app is very stiff and defeats the whole purpose of getting a “smart” app for my plant. I just wanna have apps not beg for money and do little to nothing for me in return.

title: Life savor
review: My plants would all be dead without this app.

title: I Love this APP!
review: This has helped me to be a plant guru!  My plants look better than ever!

title: Warnings won’t go away
review: I’ve had the app for a week now and it’s great for tracking all my plants. I also love scrolling through the community tab and seeing other people’s plants as well as questions they have. I’m a totally newbie when it comes to indoor plants, so I haven’t been placing them in the best places. I appreciate that the app warns me when my plant is in a spot not best suited for it, but the problem is the warning won’t go away after I fix the issue. I change the site, both irl and on the app, but the warning still being there is both confusing and annoying. I looked up on google how to fix it, but nothing that was suggested has worked. There’s a true possibility there’s a function already in the app that I’m simply missing, but I would really appreciate it if the warning would go away after I resolve the issue.

title: Very helpful
review: This app is very helpful, unlike some other plant apps. Glad I found this one. Easily identified plants, allows edits to correct minute id errors. Only negative,  Don’t blindly follow the watering schedule set by the app, continue to check your plants first or you will over water then.

title: Definitely a top purchase!!
review: Seriously this app helps so much! I get really overwhelmed keeping my plants alive and this takes away all of the worrying!

title: Schedule
review: Not keeping an accurate schedule for some plants. Wants me to water way too often then telling me a plant was sick because it’s still wet.

title: Fine app
review: Of the many plant apps, Planta is the most comprehensive one available.

title: Mimi flowers
review: I love this app it lets me know when it’s time to water my plants

title: Wrong identification
review: Mrs. T

title: Prettiest plants I’ve ever had
review: This app has helped me manage over 250 plants in my home and they are gorgeous! The trick is monitoring moisture yourself and using the advice given and the pause and skip buttons. You still need to make sure you don’t over water. The app tries to judge when it’s time to water based on the criteria you enter for each plant, but you still need to check the plants before you water, as recommended in the app. Planta never lets me forget to feed a plant. It also prevents me from over feeding. I don’t know what I’d do without it. My plants are so much more beautiful since I started using the app a year ago. There is no comparison. And I love the progress feature. It’s fun to look at the monthly photos of your plants and see how much they’ve grown over a growing season. That’s actually one of my favorite features.

title: Brown thumb to green thumb
review: I love plants so much but I had a terrible brown thumb, I killed the hardiest plants just by getting busy and being forgetful. This app really helps me a lot. And helps diagnose issues and has even helped me bring a plant back from the brink of death. Worth every single penny.

title: Great for organization with a lot of plants!
review: I love this app, it helps me organize and keep my plants watered right. I’m addicted to plants so I’m constantly getting more so this will definitely come in handy!

title: Great app
review: I just want it to keep track where you are when you are doing your daily updates and complete..you have to scroll all the way back to where you are in updates. It doesn’t save your place.

title: This App
review: I came back-and-forth with this place and no matter what this is still number one to me

title: Just OK - AI needs access to plant updates
review: The design of the app is decent if a bit clunky. For example, they have you do “plant updates” but then the AI can’t see those updates so you have to repeat information to get a diagnosis. I’d expect the AI to be able to follow along and hold the context of a plant’s lifespan to offer suggestions more automatically.

title: A+ plant care app
review: A+ app to become a green thumb!

title: Doesn’t work
review: Consistently gets plants wrong. Doesn’t identify issues

title: Not happy
review: I am not happy with this app. It does not always work well with identification and diagnosing. I have found a more reliable way. Does not make sense to continue the subscription. Waste of money.

title: Saved Money in Long Run
review: We used to buy a new plant once a month, since buying Planta, I’ve been able to keep my plants alive and they have thrived. Sometimes it feels like a lot of work, but it’s worth it to keep your plants alive.

title: Originally great
review: This app originally worked wonderfully. Since the last update, it has not been alternating the water and water with fertilizer options resulting in the app suggesting I water my plants multiple times a week. Every plant person knows that over watering will lead to root rot. I have to many plants to be checking if they need to be watered multiple times a week. I reached out to Planta support to make them aware of this problem, even providing screenshots, and just got someone who kept checking my log and telling me what the app was all ready telling me and was completely unhelpful. I gave up trying to explain to them what the problem was and just cancelled my premium subscription. I’ll be looking into different ones.

title: Helpful!
review: Super helpful and informative. I’ve never had a green thumb until I started using this app

title: Completely inaccurate
review: After so many positive reviews, I was shocked that the app could not even correctly identify my plants (I knew what they were). It misidentified most plants, including calling 2 completely different plants the same thing. It also diagnosed several obviously struggling plants as “healthy.” Completely unhelpful, not to mention that it said “7 days free,” and then charged me on day one. I canceled and requested a refund.

title: Keeps my plants alive!
review: This app has saved so many of my plants from dying! It also helps me identify them and if there are illnesses in them. I recommend to all my plant-owning friends.

title: missed two out of three
review: I had an identify three plants in my backyard. It got ALO correct which is pretty damn easy. But it called my lime tree, lemon tree and called my starfruit tree a Thai curry tree. Seriously?

title: Great for beginners but…
review:
This app is wonderful! In the past I killed a lot of plants but this app has fixed that. 

Lately my app has crashed/frozen in the diagnose my plant chat feature…it freezes every time and I have to close out of the app and go back in.

title: Not free
review: I can’t do anything with this app you have to pay a premium subscription to even use it. 👎

title: Don't pay for this nonsense
review: $3.99 a month for something that google does for free? The usefulness is nice, but it's not worth the price. There are free alternatives that work just as well or better. I'm tired of these freemium apps.

title: Good Supplement
review: I was using the app religiously without checking soil moisture levels and learned the hard way. You need to use a soil meter in conjunction with the app so you’re not overwatering, especially is you’re using water soluble fertilizers.

title: Wrong diagnosis
review: You told me the plant is overwatered. In fact it’s the opposite

title: Your AI is killing my plants
review: Newer AI version is messed up. This used to be a feature app. I’ll switch to something else soon.

title: Choices
review: Love this app but they need to add “Fair” to the choices for Plant Health.. good/ bad is too black & white!

title: Good app but could add a few options.
review:
This app is easy to use and took the place of my Vera app that’s no longer available. The reminders are great and the main reason I use the app but it’s missing options that Vera had.  If you could add those this app would be amazing! These are just a few options I loved and miss on the Planta app. 

1. Being able to add the date you acquired a plant. 
2. Being able to manually add a plant that’s not in the app without having to wait for it to be added.
3. When setting up your own watering schedule, being able to set an actual date for the next or last (either works) watering.

title: I love it it but..
review: I love using Planta to care for my plants. I would really love a social feature where users can follow each other, search for friends, view public plant collections, and share our plant journeys. It would make the community feel much more connected. Thank you!

title: Week Trial…
review: The free week trial for the app to ‘test’ it out is not great. There is nothing you can use on the app  because it will just take you right back to the subscription purchase pop up. What’s the point of testing this out free for a week when you can’t even use the app?! What a joke.

title: Don’t understand why the AI can’t do things
review: Why do I have a convo with “Dr. Planta” but it doesn’t update the watering timing or anything? I don’t get why it’s separate

title: Abusive freemium UX
review:
Most basic features are locked behind paywalls. The few “free” features are littered with ads, including frequent popup ads that require multiple steps to dismiss.

Premium offers horrendous value- if you don’t shell out monthly for basic features, you are subject to everything described above.

Recommend using any of the free or paid alternatives that respect your time and money.

title: Garden girl
review: I thought this app was supposed to diagnose my plants so far it hasn’t done that!!?

title: Great for folks with a lot of different plants!
review: Planta is great for keeping track of watering when you have all different kinds of plants with different watering needs. My plants are so much happier now that I’m not drowning/forgetting them!

title: Yes, it’s worth it
review: I wanted to have a home filled with plants but didn’t know to to take care and with this app I have been able to keep beautiful and happy plants in my home. I do definitely recommend this app

title: Genial
review: Super buena

title: Life Saver!
review: Planta is incredible. I can't talk about about it

title: Great app for tracking plant care
review: Great app for tracking plant care though think watering portion is a bit off.

title: I use it all the time!
review: This app has been super helpful with keeping the care of my plants organized. I take care of a lot of different plants, especially outdoors and I have noticed that the app is mostly accurate for the kind of care the plant needs depending on the weather. I am very impressed with it. I think I have been using it for over a year now.

title: Another good product bloated by AI
review: Did it occur to Planta’s developers that gardeners might not want AI slop in their app? I’ve canceled my paid subscription.

title: Nice
review: I like how easy it is to keep track of when to water my plants. I don’t use the paid subscription.

title: Stole Cash from my Apple Wallet
review: I’ve got the free trial and after a few days, didn’t like the app so when the trail ended I clicked cancel to paying for the subscription and deleted the app. The next day they take about 46 or 50$ out of my account WITHOUT my permission. This is considered stealing and I didn’t get my money back at all. I told apple support i didn’t not authorize or make that payment however they cannot help. This app is AWFUL and steals your money. Don’t download

title: Plants.
review:
Great app for the forgetful plant owner.
I love this app.

title: Love it!!!!
review: Great app and helps me keep track of all of my houseplants and what they need!

title: Almost perfect
review: Too many features are locked behind a paywall

title: I lost at least 100 plants because of the app
review: I’ve lost a lot of plants because you changed the fertilizer option to include watering and I didn’t realize that.  Before it was just a reminder to fertilize without the option to turn that feature off, so would just mark them as done from the group setting so that I didn’t have to go through all of them to mark as done which added a lot of time to the watering time. I lost at least a 100 plants, one of my prized possessions a huge rope plant.  The reason I use this app is because it helps me manage my collection.  I thought something in my environment had changed, but it was the app.  You need to include options to turn off features for more experienced plant parents.  The objective for people with large collections is to minimize the time to take care of the plants.
